chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara and al-Fadl Abu al-Abbas, who said: We said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

What do you say about a man who married a woman and then died, having stipulated the dowry for her? He said: 'She is entitled to half of the dowry, and she inherits him from all his wealth, and if she dies, she is likewise [entitled to half if he dies later].'

key_terms.الصَّدَاق: Dowry (Mahr), the gift given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.تَرِثُهُ: She inherits him, indicating she takes a share of his estate
key_terms.مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْء: From all things, indicating the entirety of his wealth
key_terms.نِصْفُ الصَّدَاق: Half of the dowry, the specific share due in this scenario
key_terms.وإِنْ مَاتَ: And if she dies, referring to the wife's death after the husband's

ai.seo_question: What is the wife's entitlement to dowry and inheritance if her husband dies after marriage but before consummation?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the dual entitlement of a wife whose husband dies after the marriage contract (*aqd*) but before consummation: she is entitled to half the stipulated dowry (*mahr*) and inherits as a full wife. The phrase 'if she dies, she is likewise' underscores the symmetry of the ruling, confirming that her status as a wife for inheritance purposes is not contingent upon consummation, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling highlights the legal weight of the marriage contract itself, separating the rights of dowry and inheritance from the physical act of consummation.
